title: Worksheet 3: Data Structures — Arrays
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: In programming, an array is a data structure used to store a list of multiple values together under a single variable name, instead of creating a separate variable for each value. For example, instead of creating five separate variables to hold the names of five students, a programmer could create one array called "students" that holds all five names in order. Each value inside an array has a position, called an "index," which tells the computer where that value is located within the list. In most programming languages, counting starts at 0 instead of 1, so the first item in an array is at index 0, the second item is at index 1, and so on. Arrays are useful because they let programmers work with large groups of related data at once, such as looping through every item in the array to print it or search for a specific value, rather than writing separate code for each individual piece of data.
